sit: The defender should chase the puck carrier behind the net and leave the front of the net open.
why: A player behind the net cannot shoot straight in. The dangerous space is in front of the goalie, so the defender should protect that area first.

sit: Stopping your feet is the best way to escape a defender.
why: Open ice helps you escape. If you stop, the defender can close the space, so keep skating into the open lane.

sit: The best play is to put your head down and stickhandle straight through all three defenders.
tip: Do not skate into the wall.
why: Three defenders together take away the middle. The open teammate outside is the safer play and keeps the attack moving.

sit: On a 2-on-1, the defender should skate straight at the puck carrier and leave the other attacker open.
why: If the defender chases only the puck, the pass across is open. Staying between the two attackers helps block the dangerous pass.
